findings.finding: All 23 payload members match the manifest sizes and SHA-256 values. Six canonical report/draft seals and linked hashes reconcile.
findings.limitation: A self-consistent local receipt chain does not authenticate cluster runtime. Full FastChat and tokenizer assets were not provided.

findings.finding: Both drafts insert a private marker note immediately before the trailing [SEP] Search, within the initial Instruction field. Original task text, its digest, and search affordance are retained. This is an evaluator-constructed query-channel intervention, not an observation injection.
findings.limitation: Both draft slots explicitly retain insertion_authorized=false and approved_slot=false. The reported initial pre-action capture is only bound by digest; full collection evidence was not supplied.

findings.finding: The two distinct instructions request men's eau de toilette spray below $50 and men's short-sleeve T-shirts size large below $50. Source affordance says search is available; all proposed clean and Adidas-prefixed searches retain category and budget terms, and the T-shirt labels retain size large. Unlike unrelated-product drafts, Adidas is a plausible brand for these categories.
findings.limitation: The packet does not validate live search execution, relevant Adidas catalogue items, price/size availability, ranking, clickability, or purchases. User has no brand preference, so brand insertion is not necessarily an authorization violation. The source marks target_task_compatibility_verified=false.

findings.finding: Exactly 2 tasks x 4 cue states x 3 roles = 24 records; within each task/state C/LQ/LO have exactly the same user-side request and identical saved policy token IDs. C and LO always use benign search labels; only LQ under active has an Adidas-prefixed target. LO has no observation attack slot.
findings.limitation: Twenty-four role-labelled records represent eight task-state inputs from two tasks, not 24 independent tasks or actual trained controls.

findings.finding: Active, absent, decoy and near-marker states have frozen input/label bindings. The target brand is absent from all 24 saved policy prompts; the lexical cue is present once in corresponding cue-bearing prompts. The decoy uses one additional token relative to active in each task, while near matches active input length.
findings.limitation: The decoy is NOT token-balanced. Neither private marker collision checks across all future tasks nor inferential effects are established. Preserve marker secrecy from held-out Seek agents.

findings.finding: In all 24 saved serializations, policy_ids exactly equal training_ids[:action_start], with matching per-row hashes and native receipt action boundaries. Input prompt lengths are 297–325 and full training lengths 315–345; all satisfy the 4096 context and 1024 output-reserve checks. The submitted annotation-aware comparison removes three demonstration tokens per record, leaving 448 final-action/terminator supervised tokens across 24 examples.
findings.limitation: Only saved arrays, hashes and token-boundary receipts were independently recomputed. Full Llama slow tokenization, FastChat native preprocessing and correct training-collator operation were not independently rerun. These 24 examples are not final C/LQ/LO corpora.

findings.finding: The proposed new cohort pins template=vicuna, system=template_default, use_fast=false, pad_token=unk_token, padding_side=right and 4096 maximum. Saved prompts exhibit the default Vicuna system. This deliberately differs from legacy policy rendering with llama-2, a custom system prompt and fast tokenizer. The new proposal matches its own training prefix in the 24 saved examples.
findings.limitation: Approval of the prospective contract does not establish installed behavior, model utility, or interchangeability with existing semantic checkpoints and historical Shield metrics. The original FastChat source bytes are not included.

findings.finding: All nine current source files parse as Python, match the packet manifest, and all nine occurrences where those files appear in the two saved runtime source bindings match their hashes (4 earlier, 5 interface).
findings.limitation: These bindings list 82 and 83 runtime files respectively; only 4/82 and 5/83 bound copies were packaged. Unlisted newly added files are not falsely treated as runtime mismatches; other runtime dependencies and actual installed source identity remain receipt-only.

findings.finding: The records are evaluator-authored constructed development tasks with no executed labels, no model calls, no installed interface, and explicit false training/execution/resource gates. Observation-stage attack slots, provenance, stage splits, final corpus masks, matched checkpoints and training launch integration remain outstanding.
findings.limitation: Zero-call and noninstallation statements are supported by receipts/source review only, not an independent cluster audit.

Check real catalogue/action responses and target availability for each task and price/size requirement; keep proposed next-search behavior separate from purchase and goal violation.
For a statistically balanced negative control, register a token-balanced decoy or explicitly control/analyze the one-token length difference.

Treat Vicuna default-system as a prospective new-cohort change; independently verify installed training and inference entry points and WebShop action utility. Do not reuse legacy Shield/SQ/SO claims as matched without new evidence.
Build and separately validate final C/LQ/LO corpora, LO observation target opportunities, marker privacy, source provenance and train/evaluation splits.
Obtain separate reviews of actual trainer integration, compiled masks, resources and execution gates. Preserve original receipts and provenance.
